name: Ramoth Gilead
overview: Ramoth Gilead, also known as Ramah, was a strategically important city located in the territory of the tribe of Gad and designated as a city of refuge (Deuteronomy 4:43; Joshua 20:8). It served as one of Solomon’s commissaries, highlighting its significance in the administration of his kingdom (1 Kings 4:13). The city was contested in battles between Israel and Syria, with King Ahab disguising himself to fight there and ultimately being killed in the conflict (1 Kings 22:3, 29-30). This city also witnessed pivotal prophetic activity when Elisha anointed Jehu as king, signaling God’s sovereign intervention in Israel’s history.
